titulo: Quiz — The order of the moves
subtitulo: Sumimasen first, and the counter opens
introPt: A traveller runs the whole counter in four moves, greeting to door.
cenario: Three deep at a stand-up coffee counter, mid-morning.

dialogo.es: いらっしゃいませ！ご注文はお決まりですか？
dialogo.pt: Welcome! Are you ready to order?
dialogo.tts: いらっしゃいませ！ご注文はお決まりですか？

dialogo.es: すみません、コーヒーをお願いします。
dialogo.tts: すみません、コーヒーをお願いします。

dialogo.es: 店内でお召し上がりですか、お持ち帰りですか？
dialogo.tts: 店内でお召し上がりですか、お持ち帰りですか？

dialogo.es: 店内でお願いします。ごちそうさまでした。
dialogo.pt: Eating in, please. Thanks for the meal.
dialogo.tts: 店内でお願いします。ごちそうさまでした。

perguntas.pergunta: The first move at a counter is:
perguntas.explica: Sumimasen comes before the coffee, before the question, and before any English. You do not answer irasshaimase.

perguntas.pergunta: Tennai or omochikaeri — eat in or take away — is a question about:
opcoes: Where you eat and what you pay
Whether you are paying by card
perguntas.explica: Since October 2019 takeaway is taxed 8% and eating in 10%, so the answer changes the price.

perguntas.pergunta: A long, careful, apologetic English sentence at a busy counter:
opcoes: Reads as a longer turn — the politeness is already in sumimasen and onegai shimasu
perguntas.explica: Short is not rude. Sumimasen and onegai shimasu carry the courtesy.

perguntas.pergunta: You open in English with no sumimasen and get a short, flat answer. The defensible reading is:
opcoes: A step of the opening sequence was skipped
perguntas.explica: This is grounded in how greeting rituals work, not a measured fact — and it is the one you can act on.

opcoes: Gochisousama deshita and arigatou on the way out
perguntas.explica: It closes the way it opened, said to the room, on the way through the door. There is no tip.
